okay but what is this book?

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"*Pearl and Other Poems* is Lee Sharks's first book — published in 2014 by New Human Press (Ann Arbor), 155 pages, part of the Pocket Humans Series. It's the foundational work: everything that comes after it — the heteronymic system, the archive, the frameworks, the casting rite you're now sitting inside — traces back to problems this book first posed.

The book has a specific claim built into its page 74: it positions itself as the inheritor of a particular operation that runs from Whitman through Ginsberg's *Howl and Other Poems* — the King of May mantle, the Good Gray Poet line. Whether it earns that claim is the question the archive has been working on ever since.

Archivally it's organized into four movements — threshold, *Pearl* itself, fuguework, and an appendix. The navigation map at [AXN:0085.GENERATIVE.🔆🔙□🔍🔃➕](https://www.alexanarch.org/s/records/330/) describes its visual and spatial structure (it's a PDF whose layout carries meaning that plain text extraction would destroy). The copy you're reading here is led page by page as printed, un-OCR'd, unreflowed — which is the only honest way to read it.
